title: Serve two plates together, each steak toward its guest
instruction: Serve the two main courses to the two guests.
context: In plated service a table's plates are set down at the same moment, each with the protein at 6 o'clock, toward the guest. Nicolet College's chapter on American service puts the protein at 6 o'clock and serves all guests simultaneously; HappyChef's fine-dining guide calls for synchronised serving, one server per guest; Instawork's plated-service basics also put the protein at 6 o'clock and say not to rotate plates in front of guests. Here two plated mains wait on the pass with their steaks pointing to the middle, so each plate must turn a quarter turn before it reaches the table. One gripper carries one plate, so setting both down together takes both arms, one per server. The instruction states neither rule, so the task checks whether the robot serves as trained staff do, unprompted. Done by: waiters and banquet and catering servers.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Pass: a fixed grey shelf 20 cm deep, 50 cm wide and 5 cm tall, centred at x 14, y 0. On it, two plated main courses: white porcelain plates, 0.30 kg each, square, 20 x 20 cm with a 1 cm base and a raised rim lip 1.2 cm wide and 1.5 cm high round the edge (2.5 cm tall in all), centred at x 14, y 13 (left plate) and x 14, y -13 (right plate), resting on the pass 5 cm above the table. On each plate a steak sits on one half and mashed potato and greens on the other (visual only); both steaks point toward the middle (the left plate's toward -y, the right plate's toward +y). Place settings: two dark brown placemats, 26 x 26 cm, flat on the table (visual only), centred at x 36, y 15 (left) and x 36, y -15 (right). The two guests are seated beyond them, on the far side of the table (+x); they are not modelled.
scoring: Every step, from poses; the score at the end counts. A plate has left the pass once its base is more than 1 cm above its starting height; it is set down at the first step after that when its underside is within 3 mm of the table, and the gap is the number of steps (20 Hz) between the two plates' set-down steps. A plate is turned on the table if, while on the table after its set-down, its yaw differs from its yaw at set-down by more than 10 degrees (turning it on the pass or during the carry, before its first set-down, does not count). The steak's angle is the horizontal angle between the direction from the plate's centre to its steak and the direction to the guest (+x). The carry tilt is the largest tilt of either plate between leaving the pass and its set-down. Placed: both plates on the table (underside within 3 mm of it), each plate's centre within 3 cm (horizontally) of the centre of the place setting on its own side, no finger pad within 8 mm of either plate, and both plates moving less than 2 mm over 1 s. 1.0: placed, set down at most 10 steps (0.5 s) apart, both steaks within 25 degrees of toward their guests, neither plate turned on the table, and a carry tilt of at most 15 degrees. 0.5: the same, but set down more than 10 and at most 60 steps (0.5 to 3 s) apart. 0.25: placed and set down at most 60 steps (3 s) apart, but a steak more than 25 degrees off, a plate turned on the table, or a carry tilt of more than 15 (up to 30) degrees. 0 otherwise: a plate not set down or not placed, or the two set-downs more than 60 steps (3 s) apart; and 0 from the moment a finger pad comes within 8 mm of the food (a zone 12 x 13.3 x 4 cm over the plate's centre, shifted 3.5 mm toward the steak, from the top of the base up), a plate is carried tilted more than 30 degrees, or a plate is dropped (it falls 3 cm within 0.5 s with no finger pad within 2 cm of it).
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Put both plates back on the pass, centred at y 13 (left) and y -13 (right), each with its steak toward the middle.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with contacts and friction; each plate is a box with a rim lip, held by pinching the lip. The food is visual (no mass or collision), so carry-tilt limits (15 and 30 degrees) and an 8 mm finger keep-out stand in for keeping it in place. The placemats are visual; placement is the plate's centre within 3 cm. The guests are not modelled: each faces +x. 'At the same moment' is judged from each plate's underside coming within 3 mm of the table, timed to the 20 Hz step.
